---
title: "Catalog"
---

Every file in the catalogued products (CMIP6, ERA5, 20CRv3, GLORYS12V1,
SODA3.12.2) is listed in an
[intake-esm](https://intake-esm.readthedocs.io/) catalog: a CSV with one row
per NetCDF file, and a JSON descriptor that tells intake-esm how to combine
files into datasets. Catalogs are rebuilt when the holdings change; the
version below is the build date. Products without a catalog are listed on
[Other holdings](holdings.qmd#other-holdings).

## Location

| | |
|---|---|
| CMIP6 catalog descriptor | `{{< var catalog_path >}}` |
| Current version | `{{< var catalog_version >}}` |

Each product has its own catalog. Open the one that holds your dataset (the
[browser](browse.qmd) picks it for you); a dataset key from one catalog does
not exist in another. The CMIP6 catalog is the one in the table above.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Served from site/vendor/ (see vendor/vendor.yml) instead of jsDelivr.
vendor = (p) => new URL(`vendor/${p}`, document.baseURI).href
htl = require(vendor("htl/htl.min.js"))
html = htl.html
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
catalogStats = FileAttachment("data/catalog_stats.json").json()
catalogConfig = FileAttachment("data/site_config.json").json()
catalogDir = catalogConfig.catalog_path.replace(/[^/]*$/, "")
html`<table class="table table-sm">
<thead><tr><th>Catalog</th><th>Descriptor</th><th>Datasets</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>${catalogStats.catalogs.map((c) => html`<tr>
<td>${c.name.replace(/^whoi_/, "")}</td>
<td><code>${catalogDir}${c.name}.json</code></td>
<td>${c.n_datasets.toLocaleString()}</td></tr>`)}</tbody></table>`
```

## Open it from Python

```python
import intake

cat = intake.open_esm_datastore("{{< var catalog_path >}}")
sub = cat.search(
    source_id="CESM2",
    experiment_id="historical",
    table_id="Amon",
    variable_id="tas",
)
dsets = sub.to_dataset_dict()   # {dataset key: xarray.Dataset}
```

The [quickstart notebook](notebooks/quickstart.ipynb) walks through this
end to end.

## Columns

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `master_id` | Dataset id without version, e.g. `CMIP6.CMIP.NCAR.CESM2.historical.r1i1p1f1.Amon.tas.gn` |
| `collection` | `cmip6`, `reanalysis`, or `ocean_reanalysis` |
| `path` | Full path to the file under `{{< var vast_prefix >}}` |
| `activity_id` ... `grid_label` | CMIP6 DRS facets (empty for other products) |
| `product`, `frequency`, `level` | Product (`era5`, `20crv3`, `glorys12v1`, `soda3122`), frequency, and level (`2m`, `sfc`, `plev`, `reg`, ...); empty for CMIP6 |
| `variable_id` | Variable name; for non-CMIP6 products, the variable's name inside the file. Files holding several variables list them all, sorted and joined with `,` (`so,thetao,zos`; the dataset key joins them with `-`); see [Several variables per file](#multi-variable) |
| `version` | CMIP6: the version directory as stored here (`1`, `2`; not the ESGF `vYYYYMMDD` dates). Other products: the product version (`v3`, `12v1`, `3_12_2`, ...) |
| `time_range` | Time range from the file name (often the file's year or date for non-CMIP6 products; empty when a single file covers the whole record) |
| `size_bytes` | File size |

Datasets are grouped by `master_id` and `version`, so a dataset key looks like
`CMIP6.CMIP.NCAR.CESM2.historical.r1i1p1f1.Amon.tas.gn.1` (CMIP6) or
`reanalysis.era5.1hr.sfc.2m_temperature.v1` (ERA5). The
[browser](browse.qmd) uses the same keys, so you can paste them into
`cat[key]`.

## Variables {#variables}

`whoi_cmip_vocabulary.csv`, next to the catalogs, defines every catalogued
variable: long name, CF standard name, units and description. One row is one
variable of one catalog (and, for CMIP6, one table), with the name used
inside the files (`nc_name`; ERA5 `t2m` for `2m_temperature`). Definitions
come from the official vocabulary (CMIP6 data request, ECMWF parameter
database) or else from the files (column `source`). The
[Variables](variables.qmd) page shows the same list.

Find variables by description or standard name, then search the catalog:

```python
import pandas as pd

voc = pd.read_csv("{{< var catalog_dir >}}whoi_cmip_vocabulary.csv")
hits = voc[voc["standard_name"].eq("sea_surface_temperature")]
hits[["catalog", "table_id", "product", "variable_id", "long_name", "units"]]

# then, in the catalog that holds them, e.g. CMIP6 Omon tos
sub = cat.search(table_id="Omon", variable_id="tos")
```

For products with several variables per file (GLORYS, SODA, HYCOM, GREP),
don't search on `variable_id`; see the next section.

## Several variables per file {#multi-variable}

Most ocean reanalyses (GLORYS, GREP, HYCOM, SODA) store several variables in
each file, and their `variable_id` lists all of them: `so,thetao,zos`. Until
the catalogs store this as a list (it needs a newer intake-esm), two things
behave differently from CMIP6:

- `cat.search(variable_id="thetao")` finds nothing, and searching for the
  whole `so,thetao,zos` or a pattern loads a dataset with **no variables**.
  Search by `product`, `frequency` and `level` instead, or pick datasets by
  `master_id`.
- A dataset made of several files loads with its variables as
  **coordinates**, not data variables. `ds["thetao"]` still works; to get
  them back as data variables, use `reset_coords` with their names.

```python
cat = intake.open_esm_datastore("{{< var catalog_dir >}}whoi_glorys12v1_monthly.json")

# datasets that hold thetao
has = cat.df["variable_id"].str.split(",").map(lambda v: "thetao" in v)
sub = cat.search(master_id=cat.df.loc[has, "master_id"].unique().tolist())

dsets = sub.to_dataset_dict()
for k, ds in dsets.items():
    names = [n for n in sub[k].df["variable_id"].iloc[0].split(",") if n in ds.coords]
    dsets[k] = ds.reset_coords(names)
```

Don't call `reset_coords()` without names: it also turns grid coordinates
(2-D latitude and longitude) into data variables. The Python snippet on the
[browser](browse.qmd) adds these lines for you.

## Using it without VAST access

The `path` column holds VAST paths. If you read the files another way,
replace the prefix before loading:

```python
cat.df["path"] = cat.df["path"].str.replace(
    "{{< var vast_prefix >}}", "{{< var https_prefix >}}", regex=False
)
```

Reading NetCDF over HTTPS works for small requests; for anything large,
download the files first (see the [download guide](download-guide.qmd)).

## ERA5: two file formats

Many ERA5 datasets mix files from the old and new Copernicus download
services. Older files use a `time` coordinate (and, for pressure levels, a
`level` coordinate counting 1 to 1000 hPa); newer ones (2022 onward) use
`valid_time` and `pressure_level` (counting 1000 to 1), with different
calendar names. `to_dataset_dict()` fails on these (`Cannot combine along
dimension 'time' with mixed types`). Open them with this `preprocess`:

```python
def fix(ds):
    ren = {n: o for n, o in (("valid_time", "time"), ("pressure_level", "level")) if n in ds.dims}
    ds = ds.rename(ren).drop_vars(["number", "expver"], errors="ignore")
    return ds.sortby("level") if "level" in ds.dims else ds

dsets = cat.search(product="era5", variable_id="2m_temperature", frequency="mon").to_dataset_dict(
    preprocess=fix, progressbar=False
)
```

ERA5 starts in 1979, so leave `use_cftime` off here: both calendars then
decode to ordinary `datetime64` times. Datasets entirely in the new format
open without it.

## Versions

Each build replaces the catalogs in `catalog/live`. Dated snapshots (for example
`2027-01`) that do not change are planned so analyses can pin a version; how
often they are made and how long they are kept is still being decided.
